## Chapter 1 — Things that happen to you

*Doing, and being done to*

7 lessons · 33 words · 30 phrases

### 196. Something was done to it, the easy half

**Lesson 1 of 7** · Doing, and being done to
**Can do:** Read and build a passive sentence for ichidan verbs, する and 来る, and tell it apart from what being able to already sounds like
**Grammar:** `～られる` — Something was done to it. Ichidan verbs drop る and add られる; する becomes される, 来る becomes 来られる, read こられる. The same string the potential already uses -- context sorts them.

| Word | Reading | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| 見る | みる | to see, to watch |
| 食べる | たべる | to eat |
| する | する | to do |
| 来る | くる | to come |

- 彼はケーキをつまみ食いするのを見られた。 — He was seen eating a piece of the cake in secret.
- この回線の細さじゃ、動画は見られないよ。 — This connection is too slow for me to watch videos.
- 彼らの結婚式に招待された。 — I was invited to their wedding.
- 故人をしのんで、記念碑が建てられた。 — A monument was erected in memory of the deceased.

### 197. Something was done to it, the rest

**Lesson 2 of 7** · Doing, and being done to
**Can do:** Read and build a passive sentence for any verb
**Grammar:** `～れる` — The same thing for godan verbs -- move the last sound to the あ row and add れる. 書かれる, 話される, 呼ばれる, 読まれる, 買われる. う bends to わ; る-row verbs are godan and take this rule, not the ichidan one.

| Word | Reading | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| 書く | かく | to write |
| 泳ぐ | およぐ | to swim |
| 話す | はなす | to speak, to talk |
| 待つ | まつ | to wait |
| 死ぬ | しぬ | to die |
| 呼ぶ | よぶ | to call, to summon |
| 読む | よむ | to read |
| 買う | かう | to buy |
| 帰る | かえる | to return home |
| 作る | つくる | to make |
| 使う | つかう | to use |
| 英語 | えいご | English (language) |
| 花 | はな | flower |

- 校長室で会議が開かれた。 — The meeting was held in the principal's office.
- 英語はカナダで話されている。 — English is spoken in Canada.
- バラは花の女王と呼ばれている。 — The rose is called the queen of flowers.
- そのパーティーはいつ行われますか。 — When will the party be held?
- このワインは葡萄から作られています。 — This wine is made from grapes.

### 198. Who did it, and who it happened to

**Lesson 3 of 7** · Doing, and being done to
**Can do:** Build a full passive sentence — say what happened to something, and who did it, if it matters
**Grammar:** `～に～られる` — The full sentence. What was the object becomes the subject; whoever did it, if it is worth naming at all, takes に.

| Word | Reading | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| 姉 | あね | my older sister |
| 緑 | みどり | green |

- ママに叱られますよ。 — You'll get told off by Mum.
- 彼女はみんなに愛されている。 — She is loved by everybody.
- 彼は男まさりの姉に育てられた。 — He was brought up by his strong-willed sister.
- 湖は緑の丘に囲まれている。 — The lake is surrounded by green hills.

### 199. When it happens to you

**Lesson 4 of 7** · Doing, and being done to
**Can do:** Say that something happened to you — something taken, lost, or done around you — the way Japanese says it and English cannot
**Grammar:** `～を～れる` — It happened to you. The object keeps を and the person it happened to becomes the subject -- 財布を盗まれた. With a verb that has no object, 雨に降られた, there is nothing to keep.

| Word | Reading | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| 財布 | さいふ | wallet, purse |
| 車 | くるま | car |
| 雨 | あめ | rain |
| 死ぬ | しぬ | to die |
| わたし | わたし | I, me |

- 私は更衣室で財布を盗まれた。 — I had my wallet stolen in the changing room.
- 彼は真っ昼間に車を盗まれた。 — He had his car stolen in broad daylight.
- 雨に降られてぬれちゃったよ。 — I was caught in the rain and got wet.
- 私はガンで一人息子に死なれた。 — I had my only son die of cancer.

### 200. Making someone, letting someone

**Lesson 5 of 7** · Doing, and being done to
**Can do:** Say that you made or let someone do something, and ask politely to be allowed to do something yourself
**Grammar:** `～させる` — Making or letting someone do it. Godan verbs take あ row plus せる, ichidan verbs drop る and add させる. A causee taken from a transitive verb takes に, one taken from an intransitive verb usually takes を.

| Word | Reading | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| 待つ | まつ | to wait |
| 部屋 | へや | room |
| する | する | to do |
| 約束 | やくそく | arrangement, plans with someone |
| 人 | ひと | person, people |

- 彼は家政婦に部屋を掃除させた。 — He had the maid clean the room.
- コメディは人を笑わせるものである。 — Comedy is something that makes people laugh.
- 待たせてごめん。 — Sorry to have kept you waiting.
- 恐縮ですが、２月２７日の約束をキャンセルさせてください。 — I'm very sorry, but please let me cancel our appointment on the 27th of February.
- 相席させていただいてよろしいですか。 — May I share this table with you?

### 201. Made to do it

**Lesson 6 of 7** · Doing, and being done to
**Can do:** Say that you were made to do something, and recognise the colloquial contracted form when you meet it
**Grammar:** `～させられる` — Made to do it -- causative, then passive, stacked in that order. Godan verbs contract in speech, and 待たせられた becomes 待たされた.

| Word | Reading | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| 待つ | まつ | to wait |
| する | する | to do |

- 上司に残業させられたんだよ。 — My boss made me work overtime.
- 彼は、自分の意志に反して契約書に署名させられた。 — He was made to sign the contract against his will.
- 彼に１時間待たされた。 — He kept me waiting for an hour.
- 私たちは一列に並ばされた。 — We were made to stand in a line.

### 202. By, this time for real

**Lesson 7 of 7** · Doing, and being done to
**Can do:** Say who or what did something, in the formal register
**Grammar:** `～によって～れる` — By, in the formal register -- によって (written により) naming the agent of a passive sentence. The third job of a word you already have for means and for variation.

| Word | Reading | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| 音楽 | おんがく | music |
| 弟 | おとうと | my younger brother |

- この音楽はバッハによって作曲された。 — This music was composed by Bach.
- 紙は中国人によって発明された。 — Paper was invented by the Chinese.
- サッカーのチームはトムによって引率される。 — The soccer team is led by Tom.
- 一番下の弟は祖母により幼年時代育てられた。 — My youngest brother was brought up by our grandmother.

### 203. Recognition checkpoint — closes the chapter

> A wide pass over everything this band has taught. Type the reading or the meaning rather than picking it out of a line-up. One ending built two ways, one auxiliary stacked on another, and one formal marker for the person behind it all. What is being checked is not whether you can recite a table — it is whether the right reading comes to hand for the sentence in front of you. Some of what comes back is a られる sentence that could be about being able to or could be about something that happened, and the only way through it is to read the rest of the sentence. That is the skill this band exists to build, so it is the one worth checking. The を that stays put when a wallet is stolen is worth watching for, and so is the difference between a contraction and a verb that only looks like one. Anything you miss comes back sooner. It finishes when the remaining set empties; retry as often as you like, nothing is recorded.
